title: "Research"

My doctoral research focuses on probability and the mathematical analysis of Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithms.

## Hamiltonian Monte Carlo and Sampling Algorithms

My current research studies Hamiltonian Monte Carlo-type algorithms, coupling methods, and convergence behavior for probability distributions with geometric structure.

I am particularly interested in how algorithmic design choices affect mixing, stability, contraction, and convergence rates.

[When correlated draws help](hmc-circle.html). Can correlated samples give a more precise estimate? Use a circle to see how the answer changes with the quantity being averaged, then reproduce a simulation of the exact sampler in my dissertation.

## Selected Research Themes

- Hamiltonian Monte Carlo  
- Coupling and path coupling  
- Mixing times  
- Wasserstein contraction  
- Sampling on manifolds  
- Strongly log-concave targets  
- Non-standard kinetic energies  
- Quantitative convergence bounds  

## Research-to-Industry Connection

Although my research is theoretical, the ideas connect naturally to computational statistics, Bayesian inference, simulation, uncertainty quantification, and scalable probabilistic modeling.

## Applied econometrics and time-series dynamics

The [time-series portfolio](projects.qmd) develops a practical connection between sampling theory and applied econometrics. Bayesian policy-rule comparison and recession probabilities use explicit priors, posterior simulation, and forecast information sets. Controlled autoregressive experiments examine stability, shock transmission, and the precision of time averages. A [lag-uncertainty study](projects.qmd#lag-uncertainty) carries posterior model probabilities into shared persistence summaries and finite response distributions. My [GDP forecasting study](projects.qmd#gdp-growth-at-risk) examines whether a model that predicts average growth well also anticipates the severity and frequency of downside outcomes.

Each analysis separates numerical verification from economic interpretation. The [policy study](projects.qmd#monetary-policy) documents residual and data-vintage limitations; the [dynamics study](projects.qmd#shock-propagation) identifies its findings as known-parameter simulation results. The lag-order analysis separates model uncertainty, parameter uncertainty, and Monte Carlo error, while making the supplied series' unverified generating process explicit.
